_note: The backend-swap acceptance policy for ONE named profile, as data the gate executes rather than prose a reader is trusted to apply. This file was rewritten on 2026-08-04 because its predecessor was bound only by `recorded_refine_rounds: 3` -- refine rounds alone do not name a backend, an output profile, an oracle or a DPI, and the four D2 findings it carried had been measured at a different profile altogether. `backend_parity.py` refused to adjudicate against it and said so. The refusal was right: floors measured at one full profile say nothing about another, and `--update-policy` deliberately will not migrate findings across that boundary. So this is a NEW policy bound to `pdfium/gdocs/none/refine0@240dpi`, populated from a fresh measurement run, and it is PROVISIONAL: it authorises nothing. The findings were measured at ff518be. c1cbc2a has since retired c2_paper2col (see `provisional_shortfalls._retired`) and no canonical parity run has been recorded against that tree, so this file is one run behind HEAD. The floors that remain still describe it -- that commit reports the other 15 documents unchanged on every dimension -- but re-record with `--update-policy` at the next canonical opportunity rather than trusting that indefinitely.

_ratification._note: COMMENTARY, NOT ENFORCEMENT -- the leading underscore is this file's convention for a key the tool does not read, and it is used deliberately here so nobody mistakes this block for the gate. The executable statement that nothing is ratified is the EMPTY `ratified_shortfalls` section below. These fields are recorded empty so that the shape of a ratification is visible before anyone has to invent it: all four are required, and each is checked on its own, when a shortfall is moved into `ratified_shortfalls`.
_ratification.decision: DEC-D2, on Google evidence -- not on this LibreOffice proxy

_status_note: PROVISIONAL means: the divergences below are visible, bounded and attributed, and not one of them may authorise a backend swap or a release. That is not a promise in prose -- `adjudicate()` appends a `provisional` failure for every entry in `provisional_shortfalls`, so this policy cannot report ok or release_ready while any of them stands. The findings clear in one of two ways: the defect is fixed, or a named owner ratifies it at DEC-D2.

expected_divergence._note: Empty at this profile, deliberately. This section is for documents where the two backends disagree about what CORRECT means and the candidate was verified to be the right one -- and nothing enters it without rendered evidence, because a document listed here is excused from the comparison. `c4_i18n` and `c5_graphics` were waived here under the previous, differently-bound policy, and both of those waivers rest on rendered evidence that was produced at the parity/refine3 profile. That evidence has NOT been reproduced at `pdfium/gdocs/none/refine0@240dpi`. The prior reasoning is preserved verbatim in each document's entry in `provisional_shortfalls`, where it is bounded and blocking, rather than copied here, where it would excuse. Re-verify with rendered output at this profile before promoting either one back.

margins._note: How much worse the candidate may be on a dimension before the document counts as a regression. Every gated dimension appears here, and each is judged INDEPENDENTLY -- the comparison used to stop at the first dimension outside its margin, so one improvement suppressed every regression ordered after it. Sizing: these are deliberately looser than testkit/gate.py's run-to-run tolerances, because two correct parsers legitimately differ by more than one parser differs from itself; the ratio is about 2.5-5x on the fraction metrics. They are NOT tuned to make the current corpus pass -- a margin chosen to clear a failure is the failure, silenced. dy_p50 additionally carries gate.py's 10% relative term, since it is the one dimension that is not a fraction and runs from 0.3pt to 34pt across this corpus. UNCHANGED on 2026-08-04: rebinding a policy to a profile is not an occasion to move a margin, and moving one in the same change would make the rebinding unreviewable.

provisional_shortfalls._not_carried_over: The four D2 findings the previous policy carried (01_whitepaper_market, 02_research_paper, 03_tech_report_code, r1_reportlab_report -- the core-14 font-metric class, where PyMuPDF reads a real base-14 ascent and PDFium substitutes a generic one) are NOT migrated here, and their absence is not a fix. They were measured at a different full profile; at this profile all four sit inside the margins. Their own profile has not been remeasured, so nothing here retires D2 -- see STATUS D2 and the line-box escalation ruling.
provisional_shortfalls._not_recorded_here: The 2026-08-04 measurement run reported 8 raw regressions -- 7 after c1cbc2a retired c2_paper2col -- because `--measure` runs with EMPTY margins, which is what makes every raw movement visible. Five of those eight sit inside the margins above and are therefore not divergences this policy tracks: 01_whitepaper_market (doc/word recall 0.9677->0.957, within-2pt 0.0417->0.007), 02_research_paper (within-2pt 0.0381->0.033), 03_tech_report_code (doc/word recall 1->0.9723), 05_memo (within-2pt 0.0241->0, and BETTER on dy_p50 13.36->7.36pt), and l1_word_native (live 1->0.9883, recall 0.9931->0.9792, within-2pt 0.014->0.0071, raster 0->0.0117, and BETTER on dy_p50 30.99->19.69pt). Recording any of them as a shortfall would be recording a finding the comparison does not make, and `adjudicate()` would correctly call it stale. `05_memo.pdf` and `f1_fpdf_brief.pdf` additionally stay out of every waiver section by test, not by habit: attribution is not authorisation, and widening a waiver is a product decision.
provisional_shortfalls._note: Documents where the candidate is measurably worse at this profile AFTER the margins above are applied, the cause is attributed, and the shortfall is PROVISIONAL: visible and bounded, but it may NOT authorise a backend swap or a release (plan section 17 rule 4). Acceptance is bounded in both directions by the numeric floors: worsening past one fails, and clearing the divergence entirely fails as a stale record. Ratifying one means moving it to `ratified_shortfalls` with ratified_by, ratified_on, issue and review_condition -- all four required, all four checked. The decision is scheduled for the Google Docs checkpoint (DEC-D2), because Google Docs is the renderer this project actually targets and LibreOffice is a proxy for it.
provisional_shortfalls._retired: c2_paper2col.pdf was tracked here when this policy was written and was RETIRED the same day by ebcb3be (merged as c1cbc2a), which absorbs a superscript into its host line in the PDFium parser rather than leaving it a line -- and a block -- of its own. That commit records the candidate moving dy_p50 23.55 -> 10.00 against a 10.05 reference, within2pt 0.0131 -> 0.1247 against 0.1039, and live_text_cov, word_recall and raster_frac all reaching the reference exactly. No dimension is worse any more, so the document is now BETTER and the entry described nothing. Keeping it would have been a stale waiver, which `adjudicate()` fails on by design: a waiver for a difference that no longer exists still excuses the document, and would hide the next real regression on it. Deleted rather than re-floored -- floors are recorded by `--update-policy` on the canonical environment, and no such run has happened against the new tree. The c4/c5 floors below are untouched and still describe it: that commit reports the other 15 documents unchanged on every dimension.

c4_i18n.pdf.measured_commit_source: the commit stamped into docs/evidence/canonical-gate-2026-08-04.json by the canonical run that produced these numbers
c4_i18n.pdf.reason: Complex-script raster fallback. One region in eleven falls back to raster under PDFium (raster_frac 0 -> 0.0909), and the text in it stops counting as live (1.0 -> 0.9091). Content recall barely moves (0.9832 -> 0.9748), which is the signature of a rasterised region rather than lost text. PRIOR EVIDENCE, at the parity/refine3 profile and not reproduced here: PDFium reports RTL glyphs in logical order, which is what a DOCX must carry, while PyMuPDF returns visual order, so the incumbent's DOCX renders Arabic backwards -- verified by rendering the source and both outputs side by side. On that evidence the candidate is the correct backend for this document and the live-text loss is the price of a raster fallback rather than a defect in ordering. Until that rendering is reproduced at THIS profile, the difference is tracked and blocking, not excused.

c5_graphics.pdf.measured_commit_source: the commit stamped into docs/evidence/canonical-gate-2026-08-04.json by the canonical run that produced these numbers
c5_graphics.pdf.reason: Designed-page rasterisation. PDFium rasterises one region more than PyMuPDF on a gradient/rounded/rotated designed page (0.2933 -> 0.3222). METRIC CAVEAT, and it points the other way: live_text_cov scores the incumbent higher (0.7067 against 0.6778) because invisible white text still counts as live. Text coverage cannot see contrast. PRIOR EVIDENCE, at the parity/refine3 profile and not reproduced here: the page opens with a gradient band carrying white text; PyMuPDF does not report the gradient, so the band's text is emitted white on white and is invisible, while PDFium reports the pattern flattened to grey and the heading survives legibly. Both arms are page_err 1 here, so the floor permits it: c5_graphics is the deliberately deferred designed-page limitation, and the floor bounds it rather than pretending it is fixed.

ratified_shortfalls._note: Empty, deliberately, and this emptiness is the enforcement. A shortfall reaches this section only when a named owner takes responsibility for it on a date, with an issue and a review or expiry condition -- `ratified_by`, `ratified_on`, `issue`, `review_condition`, all four required and all four checked. Nothing has been ratified at this profile or any other: the three findings in `provisional_shortfalls` are attributed but not authorised, and `05_memo` and `f1_fpdf_brief` are in neither section, because attribution is not authorisation and a gate that cannot tell the difference is not a gate.
